accepted.s: Who is associated with the theory of the vicious circle of poverty?
accepted.x: Ragnar Nurkse is associated with the vicious circle of poverty, expressed through the idea that a country is poor because it remains poor.
accepted.tq: Use direct economist–theory association and distinguish it from neighbouring development theories.
accepted.sec: Development theories → proponent

accepted.s: The ‘Big Push’ theory of development was propounded by which economist?
accepted.x: The Big Push theory was propounded by Paul Rosenstein-Rodan in 1943.
accepted.tq: Test the economist associated with a named theory rather than its objective.
accepted.sec: Development theories → proponent

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Balanced growth — Ragnar Nurkse
2. Unbalanced growth — A.O. Hirschman
3. Critical minimum effort — Harvey Leibenstein
4. Stages of economic growth — W.W. Rostow
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Balanced growth is associated with Ragnar Nurkse, unbalanced growth with Hirschman, critical minimum effort with Leibenstein and stages of growth with Rostow.
accepted.tq: Verify each economist–theory pair before selecting the comprehensive code.
accepted.sec: Development theories → proponent

accepted.s: The theory of unbalanced growth was elaborated in which work of Albert O. Hirschman?
accepted.x: Albert O. Hirschman discussed unbalanced growth in The Strategy of Economic Development, published in 1958.
accepted.tq: Use the title–author–theory linkage to separate closely related development literature.
accepted.sec: Development theories → proponent

accepted.s: Which one of the following represents the correct sequence of Rostow’s stages of economic growth?
o: Traditional society → take-off → pre-conditions for take-off → drive to maturity → age of high mass consumption
Traditional society → pre-conditions for take-off → take-off → drive to maturity → age of high mass consumption
Pre-conditions for take-off → traditional society → take-off → age of high mass consumption → drive to maturity
Traditional society → drive to maturity → pre-conditions for take-off → take-off → age of high mass consumption
accepted.x: Rostow’s sequence is traditional society, pre-conditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity and age of high mass consumption.
accepted.tq: Identify the fixed first and final stages, then arrange the intervening stages.
accepted.sec: Development theories → proponent

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Theory or approach)
a. Vicious circle of poverty
b. Big Push
c. Critical minimum effort
 d. Capability approach

List-II (Economist)
i. Amartya Sen
ii. Paul Rosenstein-Rodan
iii. Ragnar Nurkse
iv. Harvey Leibenstein

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The correct matching is Nurkse–vicious circle, Rosenstein-Rodan–Big Push, Leibenstein–critical minimum effort and Sen–capability approach.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure economist–theory pairs and eliminate codes containing a repeated mismatch.
accepted.sec: Development theories → proponent

accepted.s: India’s early planning strategy, particularly the Mahalanobis model, gave priority to which of the following?
o: Village industries before all forms of heavy industry
Heavy industry as the leading sector
Agricultural exports as the sole source of capital formation
accepted.x: India’s early plans used an unbalanced-growth strategy in which the Mahalanobis model placed heavy industry first.
accepted.tq: Apply the development-model clue to identify the sector given priority.
accepted.sec: Development theories → proponent

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes economic growth from economic development?
o: Growth is qualitative, whereas development is exclusively quantitative
Growth includes distribution, whereas development excludes living standards
Growth and development are identical concepts measured only by real GDP
Growth refers to increased output, whereas development includes improved well-being and distribution
accepted.x: Economic growth is a sustained rise in real output. Economic development is broader and includes living standards, capabilities and distribution.
accepted.tq: Split the options by meaning and reject those that make the two concepts identical or reverse their nature.
accepted.sec: Growth vs development - basis of distinction

accepted.s:
With reference to economic growth and economic development, consider the following statements:
1. Economic growth is mainly quantitative in nature.
2. Economic development has both qualitative and quantitative dimensions.
3. Economic development has a narrower scope than economic growth.
4. Economic development includes economic growth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because development has a broader, not narrower, scope than growth.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the scope statement before choosing the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Growth vs development - basis of distinction

accepted.s: Which of the following is generally used as a measure of economic growth rather than as a comprehensive measure of economic development?
accepted.x: Real GDP or real GNP measures changes in output and is therefore a conventional measure of economic growth. HDI, literacy and life expectancy capture broader development outcomes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish output indicators from human-well-being indicators.
accepted.sec: Growth vs development - basis of distinction

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Distribution is not a central concern of economic growth.
2. Distribution is a central concern of economic development.
3. Economic growth is necessary but not sufficient for economic development.
4. Economic development can occur without any economic growth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because development cannot occur without some growth, although growth alone may not produce development.
accepted.tq: Test the necessary-but-not-sufficient relationship and identify the absolute negative statement.
accepted.sec: Growth vs development - basis of distinction

accepted.s: A country records a sustained rise in real GDP, but poverty, unemployment and inequality also rise. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
o: Development has occurred because distribution is irrelevant
Economic growth has occurred, but economic development cannot be inferred
Neither economic growth nor development has occurred
accepted.x: The situation demonstrates growth without assured development. Rising output alone does not establish improved well-being or distributive justice.
accepted.tq: Apply the growth-versus-development distinction to a real-world outcome.
accepted.sec: Growth vs development - basis of distinction

accepted.s: A policy intervention aimed at the economic and social well-being of people is described as:
accepted.x: The term sustainable growth is used for a policy aim directed towards the economic and social well-being of people.
accepted.tq: Match the policy objective with the precise development expression.
accepted.sec: Growth vs development - basis of distinction

accepted.s: Which factor was given primary importance in the Western model of development?
o: High human development at modest income
Economic growth through rising GDP and industrialisation
accepted.x: The Western model places economic growth, rising GDP and industrialisation at the centre of development.
accepted.tq: Use the model’s defining emphasis to distinguish it from welfare-centred alternatives.
accepted.sec: Models of development - Western model vs welfare-centred alternatives

accepted.s:
Which of the following are welfare-centred alternatives to the Western model of development?
1. Gandhian model
2. Kerala model
3. Capability approach
4. Exclusive emphasis on rising GDP
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Gandhian model, Kerala model and capability approach are welfare-centred alternatives. Exclusive emphasis on rising GDP characterises the Western growth-centred approach, not an alternative welfare model.
accepted.tq: Separate the three welfare-centred approaches from the model defined by exclusive output emphasis.
accepted.sec: Models of development - Western model vs welfare-centred alternatives

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Directive Principles — higher national income without concern for inequality
Gandhian model — decentralisation and village industry
Kerala model — maximum income with low human development
Capability approach — exclusive reliance on GDP growth
accepted.x: The Gandhian model emphasises decentralisation and village industry. The Kerala model is associated with high human development at modest income, while the capability approach is broader than GDP.
accepted.tq: Use the correctly matched pair and reject reversed descriptions of the alternatives.
accepted.sec: Models of development - Western model vs welfare-centred alternatives

accepted.s: The Directive Principles of State Policy envisage which of the following as development objectives?
o: Adequate livelihood and reduction of inequality
accepted.x: The Directive Principles envisage adequate livelihood and reduced inequality, rather than merely a higher national income.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the constitutional welfare objective from a narrow income-growth objective.
accepted.sec: Models of development - Western model vs welfare-centred alternatives

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a valid indicator of economic development?
o: A larger share of GDP originating from the primary sector
Structural transformation from agriculture to industry and services
accepted.x: A larger share of GDP from the primary sector is not treated as an indicator of economic development. Institutional change, structural transformation and inclusive growth are valid indicators.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by identifying the structural feature that does not signify transformation.
accepted.sec: Indicators of economic development - structural and institutional change

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding indicators of economic development:
1. Workers moving out of agriculture may raise labour productivity.
2. Rising capital formation is a sign of development.
3. Social overhead capital contributes to development.
4. Human resource development is unrelated to economic development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because human resource development is an important sign and component of economic development.
accepted.tq: Identify the one reversed relationship among otherwise complementary development indicators.
accepted.sec: Indicators of economic development - structural and institutional change

accepted.s: Structural transformation in the context of economic development primarily refers to:
o: The replacement of human resources by natural resources
A shift from agrarian activity towards industrial and service activities
A shift from services to subsistence agriculture
A permanent increase in the share of agriculture in GDP
accepted.x: Structural transformation involves movement from an agrarian economy towards industrial and service sectors.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of structural change using the sectoral sequence.
accepted.sec: Indicators of economic development - structural and institutional change

accepted.s: The new view of economic development, associated with the 1970s, primarily emphasises:
o: Increase in per-capita income irrespective of distribution
Reduction of poverty, unemployment and inequality within a growing economy
Only the rate of increase in national output
accepted.x: The new view defines development in terms of falling poverty, unemployment and inequality within a growing economy, rather than growth alone.
accepted.tq: Contrast the multidimensional new view with the narrow growth-rate approach.
accepted.sec: New view of development - poverty, unemployment, inequality

accepted.s: Who is associated with the new view of development expressed in The Meaning of Development?
accepted.x: Dudley Seers is associated with the new view of development and wrote The Meaning of Development in 1969.
accepted.tq: Link the named work and year to its associated development economist.
accepted.sec: New view of development - poverty, unemployment, inequality

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT emphasised by the new view of development?
o: The simple growth rate of the economy alone
accepted.x: The new view does not rest on the simple growth rate alone. It emphasises reductions in poverty, unemployment and inequality.
accepted.tq: Use the NOT formulation to isolate the narrow growth-only criterion.
accepted.sec: New view of development - poverty, unemployment, inequality

accepted.s: A rise in per-capita GNP is recorded in an economy, while poverty and unemployment increase. Which inference is most appropriate?
o: The rise proves that economic development has occurred
Development is certain because per-capita GNP is the only valid indicator
The economy has experienced neither growth nor development
The rise indicates growth, but by itself does not establish development
accepted.x: An increase in per-capita GNP may indicate economic growth, but it does not signify development if poverty and unemployment are increasing.
accepted.tq: Apply the new-view test by checking poverty and unemployment rather than relying on income alone.
accepted.sec: New view of development - poverty, unemployment, inequality

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly expresses the relationship between growth and development?
o: Development is possible only when distribution is ignored
Growth is the end, while development is merely a means
Growth and development have no relationship
Growth is the means and development is the end
accepted.x: Growth is regarded as a means, whereas development is the broader end involving improved well-being, capabilities and distribution.
accepted.tq: Test the precise conceptual relationship rather than merely their definitions.
accepted.sec: Growth vs development - basis of distinction
